donorReadme: - Source: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute Titan Global Map - June 2015 (PIA19658)
- Purpose: Cassini ISS global albedo map for the explorable Titan moon pack
- Projection: equidistant/simple cylindrical global map, source longitudes labeled `360 W` at the left edge and `0 W` at the right edge
- Processing: cropped locally from the checked-in `4374x2430` labeled source image to remove title, axis labels, and margins, then resized to a true `4096x2048` JPEG sphere texture

coordinates.placement: latLonToXYZ in the donor src/entities/hotspot.ts, on Three.js SphereGeometry UVs
coordinates.longitudeDegrees: exactly as stored in features.json, placed by latLonToXYZ whatever the range; the donor stores values already in its own marker frame (see longitudeRange, markerLongitudeFromSource and donorReadmeNote)
coordinates.position: [radius * sin(phi) * sin(theta), radius * cos(phi), radius * sin(phi) * cos(theta)]
coordinates.conventionNote: donor: stores source west longitudes directly, without the 180 - west remap
coordinates.donorReadmeNote: - The current Titan release uses the NASA/JPL PIA19658 Cassini ISS global albedo map cropped to a true `4K` 2:1 texture. The texture itself is labeled in IAU planetographic, positive-west, 0-360 longitude, with `360 W` at the left edge and `0 W` at the right edge; `data/titan-features.json` therefore stores source west longitudes directly, without the `180 - westLongitude` remap used by some other Saturn moon textures. Broad lake-district entries are visual storytelling anchors rather than IAU feature centers.
